entries.title: Hotel Inhumans Season 2
entries.jpTitle: 『ホテル・インヒューマンズ』第2期

review.en:
Episode #2: Piano Lesson 2

"What a fantastic two-part story! After a short break, Season 2 is back—and somehow even better? I couldn't be happier."

Man... has this show actually leveled up in its second season? The way it portrayed those long, almost dialogue-free stretches, letting the piano music carry the scenes, was absolutely beautiful. And the way it delicately, often indirectly, explored the growing bond between these two boys—through their piano duets, their conversations, and the sharing of the young pianist's feelings toward his father—was simply masterful. Even the young assassin's gradual transformation was reflected in his piano playing. I loved how he became increasingly absorbed in the simple joy of spending time together, improving at the piano, and genuinely enjoying himself, rather than focusing on carrying out his assassination. And then came the inner conflict... Everything was handled beautifully, right down to the closing moments of the C-part, which is saying something, considering how critical I usually am of post-credit scenes.

The idea of continuing to send bouquets that the father himself could never deliver... There's something deeply moving about that. After all, he was originally supposed to be the one who would prevent those flowers from ever reaching their destination by killing the boy before they could be delivered. Yet now, he's doing what the father can no longer do, over and over again. Perhaps it's also a reflection of his own existence—continuing to watch over someone from a place he can never truly reach. Man, that was beautiful. Absolutely flawless. And on top of everything else, it was great to finally see not just Seiro again, but Sara-chan as well. Seriously, what a wonderful series.
review.jp:
第2話: ピアノ・レッスン2

"ちょっとした間を開けてパワーアップして?戻ってきた第2期に喜びしかない素晴らしい前編後編だった"

『いや・・・なんか2期になってパワーアップした?ずーっとピアノの調べにのせてほぼセリフのない時間の描き方も素晴らしかったし、この2人の結びつきを連弾と会話、またピアニストの少年の父親に対する想いの共有などを交えて繊細に、かつ間接的に描いていく手法が素晴らしかった。そして殺し屋の少年の変化もピアノにも現れていたり、殺しの実行よりも純粋に2人で過ごす時間、ピアノの上達と楽しさでのめり込む感じもよかった。そして葛藤・・・更にはCパート（通常はCパートには厳しい目の評価を下すが）の幕引きまで見事だった。父親が渡すことが出来なかった花束を送り続ける・・・本来は渡せる花束を渡せなくする、渡す前に始末するのは自分だったのに・・・それは父親にはもう出来ないことを自分がし続けることだし、自分の存在もそうやって届かぬところから見守り続けているということの証なのかも知れない。いやいや、すばらしかった。申し分ないです。そして今回の話では久々に生朗だけでなく沙羅ちゃんも見れてよかった・・・。いやいや、いい作品だ。』

entries.title: Even the Student Council Has Its Holes!

review.en:
Episode #3: Pool Cleaning in Swimsuits! / Good for You!

"Every segment delivers effortlessly, every character gets a chance to shine, and this might just be my favorite show of the season! Personally, the suppository and the missing panties were the highlights."

Man, this is hilarious. Absolutely no complaints. The study session for the upcoming exams was genuinely enjoyable, the pool-cleaning segment was just as good, and the whole suppository exchange during the sick visit was comedy gold—especially the way they framed that scene! Then we got the introduction of yet another familiar trope, the older sister who's hopelessly obsessed with her little brother, but even that worked beautifully. The way it all played out, right down to the missing panties at the end, was fantastic.

Seriously, this show is something else. Every single character is wonderfully entertaining in their own way, and it's just an absolute joy to watch. Come to think of it, there might only be three shows this season that genuinely make me think, "I can't wait to watch the next episode!"—this one, *The Apothecary Diaries*, and *The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity*. Damn, that's kind of crazy...
review.jp:
第3話: プール掃除で水着回!/よかったな!

『いや、面白い。文句なし。定期試験の勉強サポートも、プール掃除も普通によかったし、お見舞いの座薬のやり取りも角度も最高、そして弟溺愛の姉というありきたりなキャラ登場だったが、その流れも締めのパンツがなくなるのもよかった。素晴らしいな・・・。全員見事に魅力的だし、見ていて楽しいし、今期見たい!と思える作品ってコレと「薬屋のひとりごと」、「氷の城壁」位しかないかも・・・ヤバ。』

entries.romanized_title: Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru!
entries.synopsis:
Ume Mizunoe, a first-year student at the prestigious Fujinari Academy, excels in Japanese literature but struggles so badly in science that his chances of advancing are at risk. Hoping to boost his academic record, he joins the student council—only to find himself surrounded by a cast of quirky characters: a charismatic yet secretly shy president, a kind but intimidating treasurer, an adorably cheeky boy, and a tiny, stray-cat-like secretary.

Thrown into a whirlwind of chaotic daily life, Ume's school days are about to get a lot more unpredictable—and a lot more lively!

(Source: MAL News)

entries.title: A Tale of the Secret Saint
entries.jpTitle: 転生した大聖女は、聖女であることをひた隠す

review.en:
Episode #3: The Saint's State of Being

"Is this the real hidden gem of the season—or just a convincing fake? I can't wait to see what form it ultimately takes."

Man, this show is absolutely insane. There are definitely moments when I'm sitting there thinking, "What the hell are they even doing?!" But dropping it just because of that would be a huge mistake. This thing is seriously entertaining. Deko Akao is going all out with the writing, and Shion Wakayama is absolutely killing it with her performance. All the wildly absurd, completely off-kilter moments feel entirely deliberate, which is precisely why the occasional shift into a more serious tone hits so effectively.

And man, the animation can look downright rough at times! Monsters suddenly pop up out of nowhere and send people flying, the modern-day saint Taichi is basically Gen Z personified, and she even gets pissed off because what was supposed to be a meat feast turns into a lecture! It's ridiculous, it's all over the place, and somehow it's absolutely hilarious. Seriously, you'd be missing out if you skipped this one!
review.jp:
第3話: 聖女の形

"これぞホントの隠し玉?それともまがい物?どんな形を見せてくれるのやら"

『いや、これは無茶苦茶だ。何やってんのコレ?って感じなのも事実。しかし、それでこの作品を切ってしまったら勿体ない。これは相当面白い。赤尾でこがぶちかましている。若山詩音がぶちかましてる。超素っ頓狂な調子っぱズレも全て計算。だからこそちょっと真面目なトーンになったときに引き立つ。いやいや、マジで作画ヤバい時あるし、唐突に魔物出てきてふっとばされるわ・・・現代の聖女太一がただただZ世代だわ・・・お肉大会なのに説教タイムになったことに逆ギレするし・・・・面白いわー。見なきゃ損でしょう!』

entries.romanized_title: Tensei shita Daiseijo wa, Seijo de Aru Koto wo Hitakakusu
entries.synopsis:
Fia always dreamed of becoming a knight. Born into a family of knights, she's the least talented among them, but she still clutches to her hope and trains with everything she has. When the day comes for her to slay a small demon and prove her worth, she ends up face to face with a dragon instead! A deadly injury makes her life flash before her eyes... and she suddenly remembers her former life, when she was a powerful Saint in a bygone era who defeated the Demon King. That life ended in pain because of who she was, making her fear ever becoming a Saint again. Now that the magic from her previous life has been rekindled, she may become a more powerful knight than she ever dreamed–if only she can survive long enough!

(Source: Seven Seas Entertainment)

entries.title: #I'm Looking For a Zombie

review.en:
Episode #3: Looking for a Photo Studio

"Despite my disappointment with the first episode, this has turned out to be surprisingly good, with plenty of promise for what's ahead. I'm starting to think it might be one of the better post-apocalyptic shows we've seen lately."

I'm still not entirely sold on the way Sakura goes berserk whenever she gets her hands on a weapon, but I feel like I'm really starting to get into this show... Actually, it's genuinely entertaining, and there's something unexpectedly touching and quietly thought-provoking about it, too. Could this turn out to be an underrated little gem? The characters are all likable, and the dialogue and chemistry between them strike just the right balance. I'm even starting to wonder whether this might end up being considerably deeper and more rewarding than some of those other post-apocalyptic shows, like that touring one or *Heavenly Delusion*.

And just as the group is finally growing closer, we get that familiar zombie-story trope: someone sacrifices themselves to save a companion and ends up losing an arm. Pretty standard stuff, right? But even here, the execution is clever. It deliberately echoes the earlier crisis at the gas station, putting the same character in a similar predicament, and that parallel works really well. Now, where is this going to lead...? Man, this is turning out to be surprisingly compelling. And so that's how the whole photography storyline ties into everything! At this point, I'm pretty sure I'll be sticking with this one until the end.
review.jp:
第3話: 写真屋さんさがしてます

"第1話での失望に反し、かなり面白く今後にも期待、昨今の終末系の中では結構良い方な予感"

『さくらの武器持って狂う感じは微妙だけど、結構この作品に馴染んできた気がする・・・というか結構面白いし、何気にしみじみと感じるところがある作品無きがする。意外と隠れた秀作?キャラもみんないいし、会話もノリも絶妙でもある。もしかしたら、ツーリングのやつとか天◯大魔境みたいなやつとかよりよっぽ度深くていいのかもとすら思い始めている。そしてそこへありきたりだが仲良くなってきたところへ、仲間を救うために一人が犠牲になって片腕を失うという、ゾンビ物のお決まり展開・・・だが、これも中盤でのガソリンスタンドでのピンチと同じキャラで似た状況で被らせてきてて良い演出。さてどうなるか・・いやいや、結構面白い。写真の件もこう繋がってくるのね。これはきっと最後まで見ると思う。』

entries.synopsis:
Set in a world where 90% of humanity has contracted and died from a deadly, virulent disease, only to rise again as attacking zombies, thirteen years have passed since the "Red Day" of societal collapse. The surviving humans now live away from the big cities, still hoping to reclaim them one day. An entirely new generation, unaware of the pre-Red Day world, is coming into its own.

The story begins when Aki, who has no memories of the world before its fall, escapes her village with her close friends Haru and Natsuki to search for her missing father. As they venture into the outside world, they find themselves surrounded by zombies on all sides! Along the way, they rescue Yuu and Sakura and take refuge in a home improvement store. They regroup, and now the counterattack begins—!!

(Source: Kadokawa, edited)

entries.title: Reborn as a Space Mercenary: I Woke Up Piloting the Strongest Starship!
entries.jpTitle: 目覚めたら最強装備と宇宙船持ちだったので、一戸建て目指して傭兵として自由に生きたい

review.en:
Episode #2: Mimi the Girl

It's pretty outrageous, but surprisingly entertaining, and underneath all the madness, there's actually a decent amount of logic holding it together. Plus, the girl he picked up is cute, so that's another point in its favor. I'm coming away with a pretty positive impression of this show. I wonder if it might actually appeal to a wider audience, too? Nah, maybe not... After all, when you get right down to it, they're still screwing around. But personally, I find that kind of thing refreshingly realistic, and I actually appreciate it. I also like how whether they did it or not is conveyed simply through whether she's wearing underwear—and how, since they've already slept together, she isn't suddenly acting all shy around him the next morning. Those little touches are surprisingly good.
review.jp:
第2話: 少女・ミミ

『滅茶苦茶ではあるが、意外と楽しめるし、実はそこそこ筋は通ってるし拾った女子キャラが可愛くてよし。結構好印象の作品。一般受けも実はいいんじゃないだろうか?いや、それはないか?なんだかんだ言って結局◯ってるし・・・。そういうところ・・・個人的には現実感あって、いいと思うけど。しかもしたのか、してないかは下着を付けてるかどうかで判断、またもういたしてるので次の朝には恥ずかしがらないのもいい。』

entries.romanized_title: Mezametara Saikyou Soubi to Uchuusenmochi Datta node, Ikkodate Mezashite Youhei toshite Jiyuu ni Ikitai
entries.synopsis:
Sato Takahiro was an ordinary office worker and hobbyist gamer until the day he woke up on a spaceship–one that strangely resembled a craft from a favorite space-shooter game. With a decked-out ship, a crew full of babes, and a fantastic universe to explore, he's going to make the most of his good luck and create the life he's always dreamed of!

(Source: Seven Seas Entertainment)

entries.title: Chitose Is in the Ramune Bottle Part 2
entries.jpTitle: 『千歳くんはラムネ瓶のなか』第2クール

review.en:
Episode #1: Runaway Senpai and You

"A strange case of the actual episode paling in comparison to the recap. Or is it just me, or was Asu-nee somehow less charming than usual?"

After Episode 0.5, we finally get the actual first episode. To be honest, the recap was surprisingly well done... Or rather, perhaps it was precisely because it didn't have so much of the show's trademark overbearing, overly stylized banter that I enjoyed it more than expected. Watching this episode reminded me all over again why *Chiramune* tends to rub me the wrong way in so many little places. The production quality was undeniably impressive, though. The university, the city streets, the trains—everything looked fantastic, and the way they portrayed Asu-nee feeling nervous and out of her element after arriving in Tokyo was particularly well done. But... that's one thing, and the story itself is another, I guess.

For some reason, I didn't find Asu-nee nearly as adorable this time around, and I kept wondering why. Maybe she works better as a character when she's a little more assertive and has that slightly mysterious air about her? And since her relationship with Chitose is already so clearly defined and mutually understood from the outset, there isn't much emotional tension to get excited about. Then there's that conveniently timed encounter at the café, where they just happen to sit right next to a writer and an editor having exactly the kind of conversation the story needs them to overhear... Yeah, I wasn't exactly sold on that either.

So, all things considered, it was decent. Not bad by any means, but not quite as good as I'd been hoping for—at least not yet. I suppose the real excitement is coming next episode anyway.
review.jp:
第1話: 君と先輩の駆け落ち

"総集編と比べると見劣りしてしまう謎現象、明日姉の魅力がなんか物足りないのは気のせい?"

『0.5話を挟んでようやくの第1話。正直総集編のできがかなり良かった・・・というか本作独特のアクの強いやり取りがなくて思いの外総集編がよかったので、今回の本編をみて、やっぱりチラムネは・・・そこかしこ気になるなぁというのを再認識した。作画クオリティや大学、街の様子、電車など相当ハイレベルだったし、東京に来てドギマギしながら凄く様子の描き方はよかったがそれはそれ・・・かな・・・と感じた。なんとなく明日ネエが今回はそんなに可愛く感じなくてどうしてだろう?と思った。やはり彼女はもうちょっと強くどこか謎めいている方がいいのだろうか?そして千歳との関係性もはなから割り切ったものなので盛り上がらないし、喫茶店での突然の作家と編集者のやり取りを真隣で都合よく体験するってのも・・・なぁ・・・だったのでそこそこ。悪くないんだけど期待してたほどではなかったかなぁ・・・今のところね。盛り上がりは次回だろうし。』

Second part of Chitose-kun wa Ramune Bin no Naka.

entries.title: The Ramparts of Ice Season 2

review.en:
Episode #3: True Feelings

"Maybe this hits differently when you're in high school or your early twenties, but these days, all I can think is, 'Man, this is exhausting...'"

Koyun's tendency to overcomplicate everything is getting seriously tiresome. Actually, everyone in this show overthinks things to an almost ridiculous degree... And there's way too much internal monologue. But then again, maybe my frustration with these seemingly negative aspects is actually a reflection of my own shortcomings—an uncomfortable reminder that I'm not exactly the kind of emotionally perceptive, considerate person who can pick up on other people's subtle feelings and adjust my words and actions accordingly.

Still, these characters create far too many problems for themselves by constantly assuming the worst. And the fact that they don't realize how choosing the safest, most peaceful path to avoid taking risks can actually cause them to lose what matters to them... Well, I suppose that's pretty typical of high schoolers, too. Maybe this is simply a story that resonates more with people closer to that age, who can genuinely relate to those feelings and struggles. That said, the last few episodes have also felt a little forced in places, so I'm keeping my rating relatively modest for now.
review.jp:
第3話: 本心

"高校生~20代前半くらいだと感じるものも違うのかも知れないが、面倒くさ~と感じる今日この頃"

『コユンのこじらせが面倒くさすぎる。というか全員考えすぎておかしい・・・。モノローグが多すぎる。といった一見マイナス要素はきっと繊細に人の気持ちを察し、それに伴って行動したり発言するような出来た人ではない自分に返ってきてる不快感のような気もする。ただ勝手に自分でマイナスにしてる部分が多すぎるし、リスクを避けて安全に平和な状態をチョイスしているから失う・・・ということに気づかないのも高校生らしいといえばそうかも知れないので、そういったことに共感できる近い世代向けなのかも知れない。ただここ数話はちょっと無理やりっぽくもあるので評価は控えめ。』

entries.synopsis: Second season of Koori no Jouheki.

entries.title: The Apothecary Diaries Season 3

review.en:
Episode #51: Let Them Eat Cake

"As excellent as ever, but since this is a transitional episode still laying the groundwork, I'm keeping my rating relatively modest."

As entertaining as always. This show is simply in a league of its own. That said, this is more of a transitional episode, with the story still building toward something bigger, so I'm holding back a little on the score. Even so, there's plenty of depth here, and I love how the connections to earlier developments continue to come together so naturally.
review.jp:
第51話: 麺麭がなければ

"普段通りにとてもよいが途中階で積み上げ中によりそこそこの評価"

『いつも通り面白い。格が違う。ただし、途中回、今は積み上げている最中なので控えめ。それでも深い。以前からの繋がりもいい感じ。』

entries.synopsis:
In the aftermath of the Shi Clan's rebellion, things have finally settled down, and Maomao has returned to her old life as a pharmacist in the pleasure district. One day, triggered by a breakfast served at the Verdigris House, Maomao senses an anomaly and begins investigating its true nature. Meanwhile, Jinshi, who has revealed his true identity as the Imperial brother and begun to face his heavy responsibilities, is deeply troubled by the final message left by Loulan: a warning of an impending "disaster that will strike the nation." To make matters worse, rumors of a mysterious shrine maiden who deceives the people begin to spread, casting a dark shadow over the country of Li once again. From the depths of the inner court to the city streets, and across foreign borders—the world grows wider, and the stakes even higher for Maomao and Jinshi.

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Super Psychic Policeman Chojo

review.en:
Episode #2: Cat-Finding Senior Officer / Senior Duelist Officer

"Not bad at all—in fact, I actually kind of like it. But there's still something missing that would make me want to keep watching."

I don't dislike this show, and I genuinely think it's pretty good... But if you ask whether I'm actively eager to watch more, well... I'm not so sure. The stubborn, not-so-honest high school girl introduced here looks like she might become a regular, and I loved just how merciless Chojo-senpai was when he absolutely crushed a little kid in that Yu-Gi-Oh! parody. What a savage! At the same time, I also appreciate the contrast between that outrageous behavior and his more thoughtful side—feeling genuinely guilty about having used the kid as bait in an investigation, while also being willing to call him out for his own mistakes. That's a nice touch... But still...

I just wish there were something more that would make me really fall in love with this series. I don't mind if it gradually wins me over, but I'd like it to give me a compelling reason to keep watching sooner rather than later.
review.jp:
第2話: 「猫探し巡査長」「決闘者巡査長」

"悪くはない、というか意外と好きだけど・・・続けるにママだ何かが足りない"

『嫌いじゃないし、いい作品だとも思うけど・・・積極的に見たいかと言われると・・・微妙。今後もレギュラーになりそうな素直じゃない女子高生、遊戯王のパロでガキ相手にコテンパンにぶちのめす超条先輩のエゲツナさもよし。それとは対照的に内面では操作のための囮として使ってしまったことを申し訳なく思うと同時に事故を叱責する面もあるのもいい・・・けどね・・・。この作品を凄く好きになる何かがもうちょっと欲しいかなぁ・・・。まぁジワジワでもいいけど、見続けたい何かは早めに求む。』

entries.synopsis: In Chinjuku, the city that never sleeps, there is a psychic senior police officer who has powers beyond human comprehension! His name is Meguru Chojo! Along with his judo expert partner Nao Ippongi, this hilarious duo will keep the streets clean by any means necessary!

entries.title: The Seven Knights of the Marronnier Kingdom
entries.jpTitle: マロニエ王国の七人の騎士

review.en:
Episode #3: Recklessness

"Remarkably low-key from start to finish. I actually liked it, though I can easily imagine some viewers feeling otherwise..."

Well, this episode was about as understated and uneventful as it gets. Still, even within that quiet, matter-of-fact presentation, there were moments that subtly revealed the characters' relationships and the kind of people they are, which I appreciated. It wasn't bad at all. That said, if the show keeps going at this pace, I might eventually start giving it scores in the 7s. Personally, though, I actually enjoyed this episode's approach.
review.jp:
第3話: こわいもの知らず

"まぁ見事に淡々としていた、それでもよかったが、よくない人達もいるのだろうな・・・とは思う"

『まぁとにかく淡々としている。ただその中でも人ビットの関係性やあり方などが伝わってくるところもあり悪くはなかった。ただ、これが続くようだと7点台もありうるかも。個人的には今回の感じも好きなのだけど。』

entries.romanized_title: Marronnier Oukoku no Shichinin no Kishi
entries.synopsis:
At the center of a continent made up of eight kingdoms lies the Kingdom of Marronnier. Leading the nation is the female general Baribara, who has seven sons, each with a personality all his own.

Sleepy, benevolent, sensitive to heat, sensitive to cold, gifted with animals, proud of his swordsmanship, and always hungry—the brothers possess very different qualities, but they are united by a single goal: "Someday, we'll rescue a princess in a cool way!"

Before long, the brothers set out for the seven neighboring kingdoms as ambassadors. What encounters, trials, and destinies await them in these unfamiliar lands?

Set in a medieval-inspired fantasy world, this tale of romance and adventure begins.

(Source: MAL News)

第3話: 写真屋さんさがしてます

"第1話での失望に反し、かなり面白く今後にも期待、昨今の終末系の中では結構良い方な予感"

『さくらの武器持って狂う感じは微妙だけど、結構この作品に馴染んできた気がする・・・というか結構面白いし、何気にしみじみと感じるところがある作品無きがする。意外と隠れた秀作?キャラもみんないいし、会話もノリも絶妙でもある。もしかしたら、ツーリングのやつとか天◯大魔境みたいなやつとかよりよっぽ度深くていいのかもとすら思い始めている。そしてそこへありきたりだが仲良くなってきたところへ、仲間を救うために一人が犠牲になって片腕を失うという、ゾンビ物のお決まり展開・・・だが、これも中盤でのガソリンスタンドでのピンチと同じキャラで似た状況で被らせてきてて良い演出。さてどうなるか・・いやいや、結構面白い。写真の件もこう繋がってくるのね。これはきっと最後まで見ると思う。』

entries.synopsis:
Set in a world where 90% of humanity has contracted and died from a deadly, virulent disease, only to rise again as attacking zombies, thirteen years have passed since the "Red Day" of societal collapse. The surviving humans now live away from the big cities, still hoping to reclaim them one day. An entirely new generation, unaware of the pre-Red Day world, is coming into its own.

The story begins when Aki, who has no memories of the world before its fall, escapes her village with her close friends Haru and Natsuki to search for her missing father. As they venture into the outside world, they find themselves surrounded by zombies on all sides! Along the way, they rescue Yuu and Sakura and take refuge in a home improvement store. They regroup, and now the counterattack begins—!!

(Source: Kadokawa, edited)

entries.title: The Detective Is Already Dead Season 2
entries.jpTitle: 探偵はもう、死んでいる。Season2

review.en:
Episode #2: This anime is already dead — kidding: 'A Story of That Day No One Knows'

"Taking a five-year break from a show that was never interesting to begin with and that I couldn't care less about was probably a terrible idea. Seriously, I just can't do this anymore."

Saddly, nobody probably needs to know. So, leave it just as is...

Man... Absolutely none of this episode sank in. I couldn't muster even 0.1 millimeters' worth of interest, so I'm dropping it for now. I simply have zero desire to keep watching. That said, on the off chance that word somehow spreads that the show has actually gotten good, I might check it out again just to see for myself. And depending on what I find, I suppose there's a nonzero chance I could come back to it... maybe?!
review.jp:
第2話: この作品はもう、死んでいるーウソ→(真) 誰も知らないあの日の話

"もともと面白くもなく興味もなかったのに5年間?も間を空けたのがイケないのでしょう、てか無理"

『もう・・・何も内容が頭に入ってきませんでした。0.1ミリも興味が持てないのでとりあえず切ります。見たい気も起きないので。ただ万が一今後面白くなった、などの情報が拡散されたりした日には確認のために見て、その結果次第で戻ってくる可能性が無いこともないでしょう!?』

review.en:
Episode #2

I was going to give this one a little more time simply because it's a P.A.WORKS production, but nope. I just can't. It's awful. Apparently, it's based on a manga, and the protagonist is one of those typical Shonen Jump-style characters who's all heart and no brains, constantly spouting supposedly heartfelt lines meant to tug at your heartstrings. God, he's annoying. There's absolutely nothing entertaining about any of this. Meanwhile, the villains are just as brainless, only they're also ridiculously persistent, obnoxiously obsessive, and outrageously overbearing. I couldn't care less about this show anymore, so it's off my ranking list. This is simply absolutely unbearable.
review.jp:
第2話:

『P.A.WORKSだから様子見で残そうと思ったけど、無理。酷すぎる。漫画原作のようですが、いわゆるジャンプ系単純脳だが情に厚い発言で感動を誘う主人公キャラがウザい。何も面白くない。悪役は脳みそを使わないがしつこく粘着質で超横暴。どうでもいいので対象外。』

entries.synopsis:
Rein, an enchanter who strengthens equipment with his magic, is suddenly expelled from his guild, simply because every piece of gear in the guild has already been enhanced enough. Outraged by the absurd treatment, Rein decides to take back the enormous amount of mana he had poured into their equipment. When he casually channels it into a random copper sword, it transforms into a cheat-level weapon with 10,000 enhancement points!

With zero combat experience but armed with magic that can turn anything into overpowered gear, this enchanter sets off to enjoy a new, carefree life as an adventurer!

(Source: Shochiku)
